questions.q: The ancient Nok art culture, famous for its terracotta figures, is historically located in which present-day Nigerian state?
questions.explain: According to archaeological discoveries, Nok art originates from the geographical area that is primarily in present-day Kaduna State, Nigeria.

questions.q: Igbo-Ukwu, renowned for its ancient, highly intricate bronze castings, is found in which state in Nigeria?
questions.explain: Igbo-Ukwu is an archaeological site located in Anambra State, recognized for yielding the earliest known examples of bronze casting in West Africa.

questions.q: The highly naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads of the ancient Ife civilization originated from which of the following states?
questions.explain: Ile-Ife, the ancestral home of the Yoruba people and the source of the famous Ife art, is situated in Osun State.

questions.q: Benin traditional art, famously known for its detailed bronze plaques and court arts, originates from which state?
questions.explain: The historic Benin Kingdom, famous for its bronze casters and royal artworks, is located in present-day Edo State.

questions.q: The Esie stone figures are a massive collection of soapstone carvings representing humans. In which Nigerian state were they found?
questions.explain: Esie art, comprising hundreds of carved soapstone figures, is located in the town of Esie in present-day Kwara State.

questions.q: The art style found in Owo serves as a historical and stylistic visual link between which two prominent Nigerian traditional art cultures?
questions.explain: Owo, geographically situated between Ile-Ife and Benin City, produced terracotta and ivory arts that display stylistic features of both the naturalistic Ife and the courtly Benin styles, acting as a historical bridge.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.q: The traditional Tsoede bronzes, which feature large and complex cast figures, are historically associated with which ethnic group in Niger State?
questions.explain: The Tsoede bronzes are found in villages along the River Niger in Niger State and are culturally associated with the Nupe people, said to have been brought by their founder, Tsoede.
